item.title: Shima Onsen Valley: The Ryokan Said to Inspire Spirited Away — Guide
item.description: Shima Onsen is a tranquil, less-touristed hot spring valley scattered along a mountain river, home to numerous ryokan drawing on several distinct spring sources. Its most famous inn, Sekizenkan, dates back over 400 years and is widely believed among fans to have inspired the bathhouse setting of Studio Ghibli’s Spirited Away, its red arched bridge and lantern-lit wooden facade creating an atmospheric, almost magical scene especially striking at dusk. The valley’s quieter pace and forested setting offer a genuine escape from more crowded onsen towns.
